A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ACUS framework and USW-RBF kernel. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and equations, figures, tables, and experiments can be matched despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original AudioCaps and Clotho experiments, including captioning scores, retrieval, human evaluation, ablations, and inference timing.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical results and adds GAMA audio-reasoning experiments, component ablations, and qualitative examples.

M1.justification: The kernel, positional encoding, joint training objective, and stochastic caption generation with reranking remain substantively unchanged. Equation (14) becomes an unweighted sum, which preserves rankings under v1's stated default alpha of 0.5. The GAMA extension applies the existing Equation (13) without introducing a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: v2 adds audio reasoning on CompA-R-test and MMAU test mini, extending beyond captioning and retrieval to reasoning about sound, music, and speech. Temporal-event and event-based sound reasoning are also evaluated. AudioCaps and Clotho coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds BART-tags and AutoCap for AudioCaps, removes ACT from that comparison, and removes RECAP from both datasets. ACT remains in the backbone comparison, relocated to Table 11. New reasoning comparisons in Tables 4–5 introduce GAMA and GAMA with contrastive learning as comparators.

E3.justification: New reasoning experiments fine-tune GAMA using Equation (13), evaluate CompA-R responses through GPT4-o clarity, correctness, and engagement scores, and measure MMAU accuracy. New ablations introduce a training-only kernel condition with beam size 5 and an L=1 projection condition. The retained captioning protocols are otherwise unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds a direct comparison of kernel use during training alone versus training and inference (Table 8), temporal/event reasoning analyses (Table 5), and an L=1 extension of projection sensitivity (Table 10). Appendix A.5 adds three examples illustrating environmental context, sequential-event detection, and sound recognition. Existing ablations and examples are retained.

E5.justification: Inference timing gains uncertainty terms: v1 Table 7 reports 0.33, 0.65, and 0.81, while v2 Table 12 reports 0.33±0.12, 0.65±0.18, and 0.81±0.25. Their computation is not specified. The five stochastic evaluations, mean/standard-deviation reporting, human sign test, and Fleiss kappa remain unchanged; increased run counts are not established.

E6.justification: New reasoning results include MMAU average accuracy of 34.10% for GAMA with USW-RBF versus 30.1% for GAMA, and CompA-R average scores of 4.3 versus 4.0. Music accuracy is lower than base GAMA, 33.23 versus 34.53. New baseline, component-ablation, L=1, and qualitative entries expand the results substantially. Original ACUS captioning scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The three propositions and Appendix A.1 proofs are retained. However, Equation (12)'s first line changes from distinct sorting permutations for the two sequences to the same sigma index for both, while its expansion still uses separate permutations. This introduces a local mathematical inconsistency.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statement, and conclusion extend the paper's claims from audio captioning to generalizable audio-language alignment and improved large audio-language model reasoning. The abstract adds the MMAU improvement claim. The original unbiased-kernel and caption-degeneration contributions remain.

C2.justification: Appendix A.4 newly identifies generating about 30 candidates as the main inference bottleneck. Appendix A.3 interprets low-projection performance through approximation error and discusses the training/inference contribution. Section 5.1 also corrects the blanket claim of superiority across captioning metrics by explicitly excluding ROUGE-L.

D1.justification: v2 adds an ACUS code-access link, marks Enclap scores as reproduced, and identifies public GAMA parameters and instruction data. Existing captioning hyperparameters move to Appendix A.2 without substantive changes. Conversely, the explicit definitions of the three human-rating criteria are omitted, and detailed GAMA fine-tuning settings are not supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for GAMA, MMAU, AutoCap, BART-tags, and stochastic optimization, while removing the RECAP and AudioSet references. These are targeted updates supporting the expanded experiments; the central positioning against contrastive similarity and earlier Wasserstein approaches remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the abstract and substantially reorganizes the document: baseline and implementation material and the backbone-decoding discussion move to appendices, and inference timing becomes part of a dedicated limitations section. It also adds a NeurIPS checklist and funding acknowledgment and revises several explanatory passages.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, with widespread resizing and relocation of figures and tables. v2 adds reasoning Tables 4–5, component-ablation Table 8, and three qualitative example boxes, and updates Figure 1's displayed reranking formula. Figure 2's sampling plots are retained unchanged.

improvement.justification: The training-only control clarifies the kernel's contribution, and the reasoning analyses provide direct additional evidence about temporal alignment. Timing uncertainty, an explicit sampling-cost limitation, and code-access information improve transparency. These gains are tempered by sparse fine-tuning and judging details and absent uncertainty estimates for the new reasoning results, plus the indexing inconsistency introduced in Equation (12). Overall, the evidence supports a modest quality improvement.
